key_insight: MethylVI is a probabilistic deep generative model that accurately models single-cell bisulfite sequencing (scBS-seq) methylation data, separating biological signal from technical noise to produce robust cell-level latent representations and imputed methylation profiles.
problem_solved: scBS-seq data are extremely sparse, noisy, and biased by technical factors (low coverage, site-specific and cell-specific biases), which hampers cell clustering, differential methylation analysis, and downstream interpretation. MethylVI addresses these limitations by explicitly modeling both biological variability and technical sources of error.
method: Probabilistic deep generative framework (VAE-style) that learns low-dimensional latent representations of cells while modeling observed methylation measurements probabilistically.
Explicit modeling of technical covariates and measurement noise to separate biological signal from coverage and site-specific biases, enabling robust imputation of missing methylation values.
Variational inference and end-to-end training for scalable analysis of large single-cell methylome datasets and improved downstream tasks (clustering, differential methylation).
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, MethylVI demonstrates how probabilistic deep models can handle extreme sparsity and structured noise in single-cell molecular data, producing calibrated uncertainties and latent embeddings that improve downstream analyses and multi-omics integration.
visual_elements: Schematic of the generative model (encoder/latent space/decoder) showing separation of biological latent factors and technical noise components.
UMAP or t-SNE of learned latent embeddings colored by cell type or condition versus raw data clustering to show improved separation.
Before-and-after heatmaps or genome tracks showing observed sparse methylation, MethylVI-imputed methylation, and uncertainty/confidence annotations.
Bar/line chart comparing performance on tasks (clustering accuracy, imputation error, differential methylation detection) against baseline methods.
paper_title: Probabilistic modelling of single-cell bisulfite sequencing data with MethylVI
paper_authors: Ethan Weinberger, Wei Qiu, Wei Tian, Qiurui Zeng, Can Ergen
